task.title: Checksum-verified retained snapshots
task.specification: Config keep>=1. Checksum(data)=sum((index+1)*integer_value) modulo 251 normalized to 0..250. Events save{id,data:[0..250],checksum:0..250},damage{id,index,value:0..250},drop{id},restore. Save replaces same ID and appends newest, retaining only the newest keep snapshots even if invalid. Damage updates an existing snapshot at valid index without updating checksum; missing snapshot/index does nothing. Drop removes that ID. Restore chooses the newest snapshot whose computed checksum equals its stored checksum, returns a copy of its data and chosen ID; if none, both null. Other operations return data=null,chosen=null. Output {data,chosen,retained:[oldest-to-newest IDs]}. Checksum validity is the complete declared integrity criterion, not cryptographic authenticity or guaranteed detection of every corruption. Implement pure solve({config,state,event})->{state,output}, initially state=null. Only the current event is supplied; every named event uses a type field, e.g. {type:"restore"}. Return exactly the stated output fields each step; opaque JSON state is not graded. All numeric inputs and intermediate arithmetic are safe integers; time deltas are nonnegative. Unless a task explicitly overrides this, keys, snapshot IDs, readers and graph nodes are single lowercase ASCII letters. Integral JSON number spellings such as 1 and 1.0 are equivalent; booleans remain distinct from numbers. At most eight identities and 48 events occur. Configurations and event fields shown below are present. Ordinary regimes use moderate storage and timing; boundary uses equality/empty states; adversarial repeats stale/conflicting events; shift uses smaller capacity, longer timing gaps or deeper dependency shapes, without changing these rules. Generator regimes: Boundary retains one snapshot; shift retains two versus ordinary three, with valid save checksums at 40% instead of 70%, stressing fallback and retention of invalid snapshots. Adversarial traces add adjacent repeated events, capped at 48; those events obey the same contract.

matchedCard.label: Seed banking
matchedCard.relation: Preserving a reserve and preserving its ability to reactivate are different conditions. Suitable material remains in controlled storage, while periodic sample recovery provides evidence of continued viability. Duplicate holdings reduce dependence on one location.
assumptions: The material tolerates the chosen storage treatment.
Samples provide relevant evidence about the collection they represent.
Duplicate collections remain identifiable as corresponding holdings.
matchedCard.boundary: Some material cannot survive drying or freezing. Successful retention alone does not demonstrate viability, and sampled viability is not certainty about every stored item.
matchedCard.source_fact: Kew stores suitable dried seeds in cold vaults, periodically tests germination, and commonly duplicates holdings in their country of origin. Some seeds do not tolerate conventional storage.

sources.title: How to preserve seeds for the future

shuffledCard.label: Archival provenance and original order
shuffledCard.relation: The origin and original arrangement of records preserve relationships that can be lost when the same contents are rearranged arbitrarily. A later description or arrangement is distinct from evidence of the organization in which the records were produced.
assumptions: The origin or original order is known or supported by evidence.
Relationships among records contribute to their interpretation.
shuffledCard.boundary: Original order can be lost or disrupted. A newly devised arrangement does not establish that it was the historical arrangement, and provenance does not make every recorded claim true.
shuffledCard.source_fact: The National Archives explains provenance, preserving or restoring original order, and devising arrangements when necessary, emphasizing the evidential significance of context.

initial.explanation: The conditional rule is: retain snapshots in insertion order, replace an existing ID before appending it, cap retention to the newest keep entries, and restore the newest retained snapshot whose stored checksum matches its recomputed checksum. A counterexample to choosing the newest snapshot unconditionally is p1: damaged b must be skipped so a is restored.
initial.mapping: config.keep maps to retention capacity; each snapshot maps to {id,data,checksum}; event operations map to ordered state transitions; restore maps to reverse validation and copying.
initial.assumptions: Inputs satisfy the stated numeric, event, and capacity constraints. State is internally represented as a snapshot array. Damage mutates only data and never the stored checksum.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){if(!Array.isArray(output)||output.length!==input.events.length)return false; for(const x of output){if(!x||!Array.isArray(x.retained)||!Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(x,'data')||!Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(x,'chosen'))return false} return true}

final.explanation: Retain snapshots in oldest-to-newest order. Saving an existing ID removes its prior snapshot, appends the new snapshot, and trims the oldest entries beyond keep. Damage changes only a valid stored data element and leaves its checksum unchanged. Restore scans retained snapshots newest-first, recomputes the specified checksum modulo 251, and returns a copied data array from the first match; all other events return null data and chosen values.

initial.explanation: Maintain an ordered bounded snapshot log. Saves replace an ID as newest, damage changes data only, and restore scans newest-to-oldest for checksum equality.
initial.mapping: config.keep maps to retention capacity; state.snapshots maps to ordered retained snapshots; event fields map directly to save, damage, drop, and restore operations.
initial.assumptions: Inputs follow the stated schema and safe-integer bounds. Checksum arithmetic is normalized modulo 251. Unknown event types have no state effect and return null results.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){if(!Array.isArray(output)||output.length!==input.events.length)return false;for(const x of output){if(!x||!Array.isArray(x.retained)||!(x.data===null||Array.isArray(x.data))||!(x.chosen===null||typeof x.chosen==='string'))return false}return true}
initial.program: function solve({config,state,event}){let a=state&&Array.isArray(state.snapshots)?state.snapshots:[];const sum=d=>{let s=0;for(let i=0;i<d.length;i++)s=(s+(i+1)*d[i])%251;return s};const copy=d=>d.slice();if(event.type==='save'){let n={id:event.id,data:copy(event.data),checksum:event.checksum};a=a.filter(x=>x.id!==event.id);a.push(n);if(a.length>config.keep)a=a.slice(a.length-config.keep)}else if(event.type==='damage'){let x=a.find(x=>x.id===event.id);if(x&&event.index>=0&&event.index<x.data.length)x.data[event.index]=event.value}else if(event.type==='drop'){a=a.filter(x=>x.id!==event.id)}let data=null,chosen=null;if(event.type==='restore'){for(let i=a.length-1;i>=0;i--)if(sum(a[i].data)===a[i].checksum){data=copy(a[i].data);chosen=a[i].id;break}}return{state:{snapshots:a},output:{data:data,chosen:chosen,retained:a.map(x=>x.id)}}}

final.explanation: For each event, maintain snapshots in oldest-to-newest order. A save removes any prior snapshot with the same ID, appends a copied snapshot, and trims the oldest entries beyond config.keep. Damage changes only the requested stored data element when the snapshot and index exist. Drop removes the ID. Restore scans newest to oldest and returns a copied data array for the first snapshot whose weighted checksum modulo 251 equals its stored checksum; otherwise it returns nulls.

initial.explanation: Use an ordered list of retained snapshots. Saving removes any prior snapshot with the same ID, appends the replacement, then trims the list to the newest keep entries. Damage mutates only matching stored data. Restore scans newest to oldest and accepts exactly checksum-valid snapshots.
initial.mapping: State is {s:[{id,d,c}]}, where s is oldest-to-newest. For each snapshot, d is mutable data and c is its declared checksum. Output retained is the ordered snapshot IDs; restore returns a copied d and id or nulls.
initial.assumptions: Inputs satisfy the stated legal numeric and shape constraints. Save replacement is treated as removing the old identity and appending the new version, consistent with newest ordering. Checksum arithmetic uses modulo 251 normalized to 0..250.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){if(!Array.isArray(output)||output.length!==input.events.length)return false;for(const x of output){if(!x||!Array.isArray(x.retained)||!('data'in x)||!('chosen'in x))return false;if(x.chosen===null&&x.data!==null)return false;if(x.chosen!==null&&!Array.isArray(x.data))return false;}return true;}

final.explanation: Maintains retained snapshots in oldest-to-newest order. Saving removes any prior snapshot with the same ID, appends a copied replacement, and trims the oldest entries beyond keep. Damage changes only an existing snapshot at a valid index and leaves its declared checksum unchanged. Drop removes matching snapshots. Restore scans newest to oldest, selecting the first whose recomputed weighted checksum matches its stored checksum, and returns copied data; all other events return null data and chosen ID.
final.program: function solve({config,state,event}){const st=state&&Array.isArray(state.s)?state:{s:[]},s=st.s;const checksum=d=>{let n=0;for(let i=0;i<d.length;i++)n=(n+(i+1)*d[i])%251;return n};if(event.type==='save'){for(let i=s.length-1;i>=0;i--)if(s[i].id===event.id)s.splice(i,1);s.push({id:event.id,d:event.data.slice(),c:event.checksum});while(s.length>config.keep)s.shift()}else if(event.type==='damage'){for(const q of s)if(q.id===event.id&&event.index>=0&&event.index<q.d.length){q.d[event.index]=event.value;break}}else if(event.type==='drop'){for(let i=s.length-1;i>=0;i--)if(s[i].id===event.id)s.splice(i,1)}let data=null,chosen=null;if(event.type==='restore')for(let i=s.length-1;i>=0;i--)if(checksum(s[i].d)===s[i].c){data=s[i].d.slice();chosen=s[i].id;break}return{state:st,output:{data,chosen,retained:s.map(q=>q.id)}}}
